title: Wild, Farm & Pet Animals
keyIdea: Animals fit three care groups: wild animals find their own food and shelter in nature and should be watched from a safe distance; farm animals are kept by people for food, wool or eggs; pets are kept for companionship and need people to feed and care for them every day.
familyTip: Sort toy animals into wild / farm / pet boxes. Ask: 'Who finds their own food?' and 'Who should we only watch, not touch?' Point out a fox in a book versus the family dog.

visual.caption: Wild, farm or pet idea? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: fox finds its own food in nature
sheep kept for wool on a farm
grab a wild fox for a cuddle
dog needs people to feed it daily
watch wild animals from a safe distance

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort wild/farm/pet animals, match who finds food vs who needs people, keep distance from wild, then challenge.

kid: Wild animals live in nature. They find their own food and homes. Watch them from a safe distance — do not touch.
Farm animals live with people who keep them for food, wool or eggs — like sheep, cows and hens.
Pets live with families for friendship. People must feed them and look after them every day.
A fox is wild. A sheep is a farm animal. A dog can be a pet. They need different kinds of care.
adult: KS1 Science / living things: animals in familiar habitats and human care contexts. Categories: wild, farm, pet. Words: wild, farm, pet, shelter, companionship, observe, distance.

Common mistakes: treating every friendly-looking animal as a pet; trying to touch or feed wild animals; thinking farm animals look after themselves like wild ones; assuming pets can find all their food outdoors alone.
In the lab your child sorts animals into the three groups, matches food/shelter jobs, chooses watch-not-touch for wild, rejects grab-a-fox, then faces challenge traps for those slips.

choices: finds its own food and shelter in nature
must live in a house as a pet
is only kept for wool
practice.hint: Think of a fox or deer living outdoors without a human feeder.
practice.explain: Wild animals meet their own needs in nature; people should observe, not keep them as pets.

choices: by people for food, wool or eggs
only for cuddles like every pet
with no human care at all
practice.hint: Sheep, cows and hens are classic farm examples.
practice.explain: People keep farm animals for products such as food, wool or eggs.

practice.prompt: You sort {n} toy animals into wild, farm and pet boxes with none left over. How many animals did you sort?
practice.hint: Every toy goes into exactly one care group.
practice.explain: All {n} toys were sorted into the three groups.

practice.prompt: A set has {n} wild stickers and {k} pet stickers. How many stickers in all?
practice.hint: Add the wild count and the pet count together.

practice.prompt: If you see a fox in the garden…
choices: watch from a safe distance — do not grab it
pick it up for a cuddle
put it in a sheep pen as a farm animal
practice.hint: Wild animals are not pets; keep space for safety.
practice.explain: Wild animals should be observed from a distance, not handled.

choices: people to feed and care for them daily
no human help ever
to hunt alone in the forest always
pool.hint: Companionship animals rely on owners for food, water and care.
pool.explain: Pets depend on people for daily care — unlike wild animals.

pool.prompt: Calling every animal a pet is…
choices: a mistake — wild and farm groups differ
always correct
required by science
pool.hint: Foxes and sheep are not the same care group as a house dog.
pool.explain: Wild, farm and pet are different categories with different care rules.

choices: is a farm animal kept for wool or food
is always a wild animal with no people
must be a house pet
pool.hint: Farms keep animals for products such as wool.
pool.explain: Sheep are classic farm animals cared for by people for products.

pool.prompt: Why keep distance from wild animals?
choices: they look after themselves and can be unsafe to touch
they are secretly all pets
farms forbid watching nature
pool.hint: Observe wildlife; do not treat it like a cuddly pet.
pool.explain: Wild animals meet their own needs and should not be approached for cuddles.

pool.prompt: Three boxes hold wild, farm and pet. You place {n} animals, one group each round for {n} rounds. How many placed?
pool.hint: Each placement adds one animal to a group.
pool.explain: You placed {n} animals across the care groups.

pool.prompt: A poster shows {n} farm animals and you add {k} pet photos. How many animals on the poster now?
pool.hint: Add the farm count and the new pet photos.

pool.prompt: A dog that lives in a house for friendship is…
choices: a pet
always a wild animal
only a farm sheep
pool.hint: Companionship at home is the pet category.
pool.explain: House dogs kept for companionship are pets.

pool.prompt: Farm animals looking after themselves with no people…
choices: mixes them up with wild animals
is the farm definition
means they are pets
pool.hint: Farm animals are kept and cared for by people.
pool.explain: Self-sufficient living in nature describes wild animals, not farm stock.
